messages:
julia (solutions): Heads-up — partner sent a draft contract clause that mandates explicit per-event ACKs for marketplace usage events. They want a 30s ack SLA and notification on any failed delivery. Thoughts?
kevin (billing): 30s seems tight for cross-region si->us ingestion. What's their retry/backoff expectation?
sam (eng): technically we ack on receipt into the ingestion queue immediately. End-to-end delivery to ledger can be async. Is partner expecting guaranteed write to billing ledger within 30s or just an HTTP 200 on webhook?
maria (partnerships): Partner language is ambiguous — they called it "acknowledgement of ingestion". I'll push them for precise definition but we should propose a pragmatic contract.
julia (solutions): Proposal: we provide an HTTP 200 within 2s on valid payload and emit a delivery event (event_id + status) when it lands in staging ledger within 5 minutes. If ledger write fails, we notify partner via webhook with failure code and retries. Agree? :thinking_face:
kevin (billing): That maps to our current SLA capabilities. We should add a formal enum of statuses: RECEIVED, QUEUED, WRITTEN, FAILED. Partner can subscribe to status webhooks.
sam (eng): Implementation notes: we can return 200 after validation and push to kafka topic. Add an at-least-once consumer that writes to ledger and emits `WRITTEN` or `FAILED`. For retries we have exponential backoff up to 1hr. Example header we can echo: `X-Redwood-Event-Id: <uuid>` and `X-Redwood-Status-Url: /v1/partners/events/<id>/status`.
jeulia (solutions): small typo — that's me :) Also add idempotency key requirement from their side to avoid dup billing. Suggest `X-Partner-Idempotency-Key`.
kevin (billing): Agree on idempotency. Billing needs to dedupe within 24h window. We'll document dedupe semantics and failure codes (400 malformed, 409 duplicate, 500 transient).
eve (legal): From contract perspective, avoid hard SLA penalties on the 30s path. Suggest we accept notification SLA for RECEIVED (2s) and an expected WRITTEN window (5min best-effort), with credits only if WRITTEN misses by >24h and is due to Redwood fault.
maria (partnerships): I'll share that redline to partner and propose webhooks for status. Also ask if they need an async pull endpoint to reconcile (we have `GET /partner/events?since=`).
julia (solutions): Good call. Also include a reconciliation report format (CSV/Parquet) daily with columns: event_id, timestamp_received, status_history, tokens_consumed, plan_id. Partners love CSV.
sam (eng): Logging snippet for status emitter (for ops):
```
INFO [ingest] event_id=7f3a2e received=true queued=true written=true duration_ms=312
ERROR [ingest] event_id=9b1c4f write_failed=true retries=5 last_err=timeout
```
kevin (billing): We should add a metric `partner_event_write_latency` and an alert if p95 > 1min for a given partner. Ops needs that.
maria (partnerships): Ok I'll draft the SLA section and a short tech appendix with headers and example payloads. Sending to partner this afternoon. Will loop in @kevin and @sam on the redline.
ingest-bot: automated: subscription "partner-xyz" webhook registered at https://hooks.partner-xyz.example/ack-status (verified) :white_check_mark:
julia (solutions): Thanks — once they accept, we'll schedule a quick runbook for oncall to handle FAILED states and customer escalations. :thumbsup:
